sources.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, first edition
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 19, §§19.1–19.7; printed pp. 509–528 (PDF pp. 529–548). The sections on local polynomial approximations, second-order models, stationary-point classification, CCD construction, and model-adequacy cautions were read in full.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §§19.1–19.2: response-surface aims and low-order polynomial models as local approximations on a declared factor region
contents.reason: The local definition records the region-specific approximation convention and explicitly makes no physical-polynomial or outside-region claim.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §§19.3–19.4: first-order design, center-point pure error, lack-of-fit tests, and steepest-ascent analysis
contents.reason: The assigned pair does not claim first-order lack-of-fit testing, pure-error inference, or steepest-ascent procedures; no such result is used in the CCD definition or stationary-point theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.5: second-order model form, stationary-point formula, and eigenvalue-sign classification
contents.reason: The source gives the model and canonical classification; the item derives the differential and the eigenvalue cases locally and restricts application to the fitted region.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.6: factorial or fractional factorial core together with axial and center runs in a central composite design
contents.reason: The definition uses these three run components and records the standard second-order fractional-core resolution condition.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.6: rotatability, uniform precision, orthogonal blocking tables, and Box–Behnken alternatives
contents.reason: The assigned contract defines a CCD but claims no rotatability, uniform-precision, blocking, or Box–Behnken property.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.7: canonical analysis of fitted coefficients and warning that an estimated stationary point can have substantial uncertainty
contents.reason: The theorem is conditional algebra for supplied coefficients; its Remarks state that it neither establishes model adequacy nor quantifies uncertainty in an estimated stationary point.

contents.name: Examples 19.1–19.4: cake-baking data, fitted regressions, and software canonical-analysis output
contents.reason: The B examples use a newly specified exact saddle model and a finite candidate design; no cake data, regression output, or software calculation is reused.

sources.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization (2004)
sources.locator: Complete §3.1.5, PDF pp. 87–88 / printed pp. 73–74, including the log-determinant line-restriction proof; complete §7.5, PDF pp. 399–406 / printed pp. 385–392, including relaxed designs, D/A/E criteria, duality, and extensions.

contents.name: §3.1.5: log-determinant concavity proved by restricting to a positive-definite line segment
contents.reason: The item supplies a full local proof from the determinant differential, inverse derivative, trace identity, and spectral decomposition.

contents.name: §7.5: linear measurement model, information matrix, relaxed weight simplex, and D/A/E criteria
contents.reason: The definition states the finite candidate set, weight constraints, information matrix, nonsingular domain, and each requested criterion.

contents.name: §7.5: variance of a specified linear functional from the error covariance matrix
contents.reason: The fixed-vector c criterion is stated locally as c^T M^{-1}c; the page does not claim a covariance theorem beyond the supplied model contract.

contents.name: §7.5: relaxed approximate allocations versus integer run counts and the D-optimal objective
contents.reason: The example proves the difference by a complete three-candidate, three-run enumeration rather than importing a rounding heuristic.

contents.name: §7.5: dual ellipsoid and complementary-slackness discussion for optimal designs
contents.reason: The assigned proof route is a direct directional-derivative necessity argument plus local log-determinant concavity; no dual attainment or complementary-slackness theorem is assumed.

contents.name: §7.5.3: resource constraints and experiments returning multiple measurements
contents.reason: The assigned candidate-set model has no budget constraints or matrix-valued measurement choices, so these extensions are not asserted.

sources.title: Gary W. Oehlert, A First Course in Design and Analysis of Experiments, first edition
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 19, §§19.5–19.7; printed pp. 517–528 (PDF pp. 537–548), with the second-order saddle discussion, CCD example, canonical analysis, and uncertainty caveat read in full.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.5 and Figure 19.3: a quadratic saddle has directions of increase and decrease
contents.reason: The example verifies both signs directly along the two eigen-directions in the declared region.

contents.name: Example 19.3: cake-baking CCD augmentation and observed response values
contents.reason: No source-specific observations or empirical conclusion are reused; the local B example is a symbolic finite design calculation.

contents.name: Chapter 19 §19.7: uncertainty of an estimated canonical stationary point
contents.reason: The theorem Remarks distinguish exact classification of supplied fitted coefficients from uncertainty in estimating those coefficients.

sources.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization (2004)
sources.locator: Complete §7.5, PDF pp. 399–406 / printed pp. 385–392; the discrete integer allocation and relaxed approximate-weight distinction were read in full.

contents.name: §7.5.1: integer run counts versus the relaxed approximate-design simplex
contents.reason: The example enumerates all ten integer count triples at n=3 and compares their maximum determinant with a feasible approximate design.

contents.name: §7.5.2: D/A/E scalarizations and their candidate-dependent information objectives
contents.reason: The A page defines the four criteria on the same stated finite model and expressly does not claim they give a common ranking.

contents.name: Figures 7.9–7.12: the book-specific twenty-vector example and plotted confidence ellipsoids
contents.reason: The B example uses candidates {0,1,2} and supplies every matrix and integer allocation locally; no plotted weights or figure conclusion is reused.
